title: King Azott
text: “Hmm… so you noticed after all. Perhaps this was overdoing it a bit. What with public safety declining, I’ve had my hands full cleaning up one mess after another, and one body simply isn’t enough.”
“What do you mean by that!?”
“Nothing complicated. Rafumi-chan split into copies and disguised herself as me to solve problems all over the country. Well, Heroes do have teleportation at their disposal, so…”

The documents Father had produced recorded Ren’s various heroic exploits, but multiple incidents had occurred simultaneously in different locations—and every single one of them credited Ren with the resolution, I say.
“Well, there’s also a lot of gossip floating around Melromarc about criminals impersonating me, so I figure a lot of people haven’t caught on yet.”
“Impersonators are one thing, but when the one who resolves every incident is always the same person, that gets suspicious fast. So it was Rafumi-san all along…”
Itsuki let out a sigh, seeming to accept this explanation.
“There’s no reason it had to be done in my form! Couldn’t she have just disguised herself as Itsuki and solved things that way!?”
“Too much trouble, so I didn’t bother. Azott, you are now the most famous Hero in the world.”
“That makes me absolutely miserable!”
“Well, becoming famous for accomplishments that aren’t even yours does sound unpleasant… As someone whose reputation is entirely bad, I’m almost a little jealous.”

Father’s bad reputation in Melromarc was practically boundless, I say. It was as if the people of Melromarc unconsciously believed that every misfortune in the world was the Shield Hero’s fault, even though he had, quite literally, done nothing wrong. The Waves themselves were somehow blamed on the Shield Hero in Melromarc, indeed. Some sort of wicked god, was it? That “wicked god” was in fact none other than the Crimson Swine’s true form. Ark had humbled himself, calling himself a god-hunter—something that, to the faithful, would look like a wicked god in his own right—but that man was nothing of the sort. He was one who delivered just retribution upon gods who inflicted senseless cruelty, one who sought to save the people. After all, it was he who had freed me from a world bound by irrationality.
“The newspapers run photos and illustrations, you know… and since a member of Ren’s party usually shows up standing right next to him in most of them, it might be easier to spot than you’d think.”
Ren poked a hand out from Luna-chan’s feathers, flipped through the papers, and began to tremble.
“Ah, yes—each companion paired individually, with Azott, that is, myself, splitting apart to act independently.”
“Those guys—!”
“So, in other words… Ren’s multiplied into about four, I’d guess?”
“Naive, Shield Hero. You’ve forgotten Kuro.”
“Ah… five, then.”
The peace of Melromarc, it turned out, was being maintained by five Rens, I say.
“Aaah, Time Drive and Aegis! The Jet-Black Fang and Claw, Kuro, sensing the Destiny Time alongside the Dark Holy Hero, has arrived, hear me roar!”
Kuro-chan came dashing up, carrying Ren atop her. As ever, her choice of words remained needlessly elaborate, I say. Was this level of chaos really necessary?
“There was also the Pet Dog—Dark Swordsman?—having fun with Luna.”
“I am NOT having fun!”
Ren yipped and yapped like a small dog. Really, wasn’t this getting a bit too noisy?
“Kuro-chan looks like she’s having a blast. Does she get to play with Rafumi-chan a lot?”
“Yep! The Illusion, Dark Holy Hero, repeats her battle to return the twilight world of the rotting gods to darkness, alongside the Jet-Black Fang and Claw—”
“How shall I put this… that sounds like an exhaustingly troublesome Filolial.”
“Ahaha… still, I bet Kuro-chan and the current you could get along pretty well, Itsuki.”
“Please, spare me. That sounds thoroughly exhausting. Ren-san alone is more than enough.”
“Hey! You— I have absolutely no intention of playing along with this nonsense!”
“Well, right now you’re a bit too tangled up with Luna-chan to have much say in the matter, aren’t you?”
Itsuki, perched atop Father’s shoulders, let out a little snicker as he mocked Ren, I say.
“Itsuki! You—!”
Ren, mortified at being laughed at, bristled with indignation, indeed.
“Now, now… let’s give Ren some credit for all his hardships, Itsuki.”
“You’re the one who’s beloved by all sorts of people and gets to be happy about it.”
“You call THIS happiness!?”
And yet, thinking of the company Itsuki kept, it was, admittedly, undeniable that Ren had the better deal, I say.
“Ren-sama, did you call for us?”

And with that, Ren’s companions came shuffling over in a great swarm, I say. Naturally, among them were the various Rafumis disguised as Ren, each and every one. Leading the pack, as always, seemed to be the one hailing from the Chocolate region. Incidentally, the number two in Ren’s party was apparently of noble birth—and had a remarkable knack for slipping past Itsuki’s watchful gaze, I say.
“Fuh!”
In perfect unison, all the Rafumis disguised as Ren struck the exact same pompous, self-satisfied pose.
“I mean… when five copies of the same person gather together like that, it starts feeling like some kind of joke, doesn’t it? Almost funny.”
“Five Ren-sans. That does feel like it could be the setup for some kind of story.”
“Right? Like, the original dog-Ren could be the straight man, and the one riding with Kuro-chan is Number One, the next is Number Two, then Number Three, and so on.”
“That’s a fine idea, but… wasn’t there something like that in an old anime or manga? Septuplets, or was it octuplets?”

“Ah, yeah, I think there was one like that that got remade into a big hit, if I recall right. Once Ren gets back to normal, maybe the six of them could form an idol group? If each one shows some individuality, it might really take off.”
“Or perhaps something like several players all cosplaying the same famous anime protagonist and matching their looks to fit.”
“Ahh… yeah, that tracks. Ren does have that vibe about him. Maybe that’s even where the name Azott comes from… nah, that’s probably too much of a stretch.”
“Shut up, both of you! We are getting horrendously off topic! And that name is NOT based on some anime!”

Ren, face twisted in fury, barked and yipped from within Luna-chan’s chest fluff. Apparently he had some real attachment to that name. If I recalled correctly, it was modeled after the Azoth Sword—supposedly a blend of “alchemy” and “alchemist’s blade,” or something along those lines.

“Well, with the real Ren acting like this, I don’t know if that idol thing’s gonna work out. Still cute, though… Oh, but now that I think about it, there could totally be a story where the real him can’t show his face anymore, so his doubles have to act in his place—total slapstick chaos. Like those hero shows where a copy robot takes over for the hero.”
“Enough of that, hurry up and revert already! Rafumi! Or Naofumi’s going to keep rambling about his nerdy hobbies forever!”
“Nerdy hobbies, how rude—”
“Very well.”
Obeying Ren’s command, Rafumi gathered all five Ren body-doubles into a single spot, I say. Then Father spoke up.
“Wh-what!? …The Rens are—!?”
With a puff, the Ren doubles all merged together in a cloud of smoke, becoming a single Ren doppelganger.
“The Rens are merging together, one after another! Behold—King Ren has been born!”
This was a reference only Father himself would understand, I say. I awaited his explanation.
“Naofumi! What in the world is that reference!”
“Oh, y’know… something about gathering together and becoming one just made me think of a certain game’s slime enemy. Rafumi-chan was originally some kind of chocolate, liquid-type monster, right?”

Some vague design I’d seen once, long ago in Japan, floated up in the back of my mind, indeed. So such strange monsters did exist. Well, I supposed it was a fittingly Rafumi-like flourish for a fusion sequence.
“Naofumi! Just how deep does your stock of these references go!”
“Hmm… well put. In that case, shall we call this form King Azott?”

“Countless fake Rens, and the king among all the Azotts—so, King Azott! Man, that really does sound like something out of a hardcore gamer’s vocabulary—makes me wonder if Ren back in his gaming days was actually like this, huh?”
“SHUT UUUUUUP! Grrrgh! Hundred Sword!”
With a *shwip*, Ren somehow managed to draw his sword from within Luna-chan’s feathers and hurl it at the Rafumi now calling herself King Azott, indeed. But she dodged it in a flash.
“Fuh… did you truly believe an attack of that caliber could ever reach King Azott?”
“Ohh, a Graceful Evasion—Illusion Dance!”
Kuro-chan’s naming sense was really something else, indeed.
“Would you all knock it off already.”
Ren yipped and yapped, radiating pure murderous intent.
“Well, if we keep messing with Ren any more he might actually kill someone for real. Rafumi-chan, could I get you to handle seeing Melty-chan off?”
“Of course. All the arrangements on our end are finished as well. As for the bounty situation, we’ve worked out a plan to suppress it completely.”
The leader of Ren’s party spoke up to us, sounding a bit worried, indeed.

“I was quite startled, you know. Suddenly hearing that the Shield Hero and company, to whom we’d entrusted Ren-sama, had been placed under a bounty, followed by a request to rescue the Second Princess.”
Then the leader of Ren’s companions turned to speak to Ren himself, indeed.
